assertion_analysis.assertions: len(stored)==1; judge_kind==jev; is_canonical is False; score is None; cascade:route==refine
assertion_analysis.fails_if: The store writes zero or multiple rows, loses the Jev kind, marks the row canonical, writes a scalar score, or omits the route, respectively.
The direct result loses or changes that check ID, or the manually supplied check probability no longer triggers fanout; removing the workers.py handoff does not fail either assertion.
The production note again substitutes its reconstructed generic claim for contradiction_reason; the base log shows this exact failure.
build_docs_audit_report bypasses run_house_style_checks when conventions are supplied; the base log shows this exact failure.

assertion_analysis.assertions: at threshold routes accept; epsilon below routes chat
assertion_analysis.fails_if: The route stops using the supplied threshold edge correctly; a changed threshold artifact moves both the test input and router cutoff and does not fail these assertions.

assertion_analysis.assertions: at cutoff routes refine; failed_checks equals chosen ID; epsilon below with high acceptance routes accept
assertion_analysis.fails_if: The first configured check is ignored, its ID is lost, or its comparator mishandles the edge; a changed first cutoff moves both test input and router cutoff.
A check-clear score just under acceptance stops routing to chat; a changed accept cutoff moves the test input with it and no reject edge is tested.
adjudicate_review fails to call its mocked store, omits either incumbent model, or replaces the mocked incumbent score; removing either production workers.py call site would not fail it.

assertion_analysis.assertions: calls equals expected_calls; winning_score equals expected_score; refine carries first failed check ID
assertion_analysis.fails_if: adjudicate_review invokes the mocked incumbent on an accept/refine, invokes more than the first chat model, returns another direct score, or drops the mocked failed check; later graph_ops stage refusal is never reached.

findings.text: blocking: Direct accept and refine return jev_cascade_* methods, which graph_ops.py:16961-16972 treats as quorum shortfalls; direct accepts are parked and name refinements are ineligible, so the deciding mode cannot deliver its stated routes.

blocking: A check-clear score below reject_threshold goes to chat even though the plan and brief reserve chat for the uncertain band; the committed evidence fragment acknowledges the out-of-band fallback and no test asserts the reject boundary.

blocking: A refused lease or failed Jev call leaves the default chat route and cascade.py:334 stores it as a judgment-backed shadow route with empty answers, corrupting route-share measurements with cases that were never judged.

follow-on: The accept and check threshold tests read the same committed cutoff values that the router reads, so changing a cutoff in cascade_thresholds.json moves their inputs and expected results together and leaves them green.

follow-on: The trigger test constructs check_results itself from the direct result and calls should_trigger_fanout directly; deleting workers.py:7272-7330, the production handoff to refinement, would leave this assertion green.
